a new approach for the detection of focal lesions in the cerebral vasculature by means of multiphase contrast-enhanced 2D and 3D-MRA.
the development of a new contrast-enhanced, 3D-MRA-sequence for focal lesion detection in patients with suspected renal arterial disease.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
contrast-enhanced 2D-MR angiograms are the method of choice in the diagnosis of intracranial vascular lesions.
the use of 3D-CE-MRA in the evaluation of patients with focal lesions in the peripheral vascular system is a valuable diagnostic tool in comparison to conventional angiography.
multiphase, contrast enhanced 3D MRA is a useful tool for the detection, localization, and characterization of focal lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multiphase, contrast enhanced 3D-MRA is a very useful tool for morphological and functionally oriented diagnosis of focal lesions.
the combination of a multiphase 3D-MRA with a 3D-FLAIR sequence and a contrast-enhanced 2D-MRI sequence allows for a complete morphologic and functional assessment of focal brain lesions.
the combination of 3D-MRA with 3D-MIP and 3D-MPR techniques provides an excellent overview of the arterial and venous system.

, while the 3D MR angiography technique is very sensitive in detecting the presence of a focal lesion, it is not very specific in identifying its nature.
the use of 3D contrast-enhanced MRI angiography is an accurate method for the morphological and functional detection of focal lesions in patients with peripheral arterial disease.
